title: Go: Rate Limiter
description: Build a production-grade rate limiter in Go with sliding window and token bucket algorithms using mutexes and timers.

steps.title: Atomic counter with mutex
steps.description: Create a `Counter` struct with `sync.Mutex` that tracks request counts within a time window. Implement `Increment()` and `Reset()` methods. In a loop, increment the counter 10 times, print the count after each increment, then reset and print the count again.
hints: Embed `sync.Mutex` in the struct and guard reads/writes with `Lock()`/`Unlock()`
Use `defer c.Unlock()` after locking to ensure release

verification.successMessage: Thread-safe counter with mutex correctly tracks and resets counts!
verification.failureMessage: Print the count after each increment and after reset using fmt.Printf.

steps.title: Sliding window log
steps.description: Implement a `SlidingWindow` limiter that stores timestamps of requests in a slice. On each request, remove timestamps older than the window duration and check if the count exceeds the limit. Print "Allowed" or "Denied" for 6 rapid requests with a limit of 3 per second.
hints: Store `[]time.Time` in the struct and prune old entries with a helper method
Use `time.Now()` for the current timestamp and a configurable window duration
Use `time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)` between some requests to demonstrate window sliding

verification.successMessage: Sliding window log correctly allows within limit and denies excess requests!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'Allowed' for requests within the limit and 'Denied' for requests exceeding it.

steps.title: Token bucket algorithm
steps.description: Implement a `TokenBucket` with a capacity and refill rate. Use a goroutine with `time.Ticker` to periodically add tokens. The `Take()` method consumes a token and returns true, or false if the bucket is empty. Print the result of 8 consecutive `Take()` calls with a capacity of 5.
hints: Create a `time.Ticker` that refills one token per tick up to capacity
Use a `chan struct{}` or a counter with mutex to track available tokens
Start the refill goroutine in `NewTokenBucket` and stop the ticker when done

verification.successMessage: Token bucket fills over time and correctly rejects when empty!
verification.failureMessage: Print 'true' when Take() succeeds and 'false' when the bucket is empty.

steps.title: Per-client rate limiter
steps.description: Build a `ClientLimiter` that manages separate token buckets per client ID using a `map[string]*TokenBucket` with a mutex. Implement `GetLimiter(clientID)` that creates a new bucket if one doesn't exist. Test with two clients making requests and print "Client X: Allowed" or "Client X: Denied".
hints: Guard the map with `sync.RWMutex` — use `RLock()` for reads and `Lock()` for writes
Use `defer r.Unlock()` pattern consistently to avoid deadlocks
Print client-specific results so each client's limit is clearly visible

verification.successMessage: Per-client rate limiter isolates limits correctly between different clients!
verification.failureMessage: Print each request result with the client ID, e.g. 'Client A: Allowed'.

steps.title: HTTP middleware wrapper
steps.description: Create an `HTTPRateLimiter` middleware that wraps `http.Handler`. Use the per-client limiter keyed by IP address. For denied requests, write a 429 status and "Rate limit exceeded" response. Test with a simple handler and print the response status codes from multiple rapid requests.
hints: Client IP can be extracted from `r.RemoteAddr`
Use `http.StatusTooManyRequests` (429) for denied requests and `http.StatusOK` (200) for allowed

verification.successMessage: HTTP middleware correctly returns 200 for allowed and 429 for rate-limited requests!
verification.failureMessage: Print the HTTP status codes returned for each request using fmt.Println.
